title: Add RAG Recipe Cookbook: interactive multi-index notebook + live assertion harness
author: Priya Kumar
release_notes: Add a new RAG Recipe Cookbook with an interactive notebook and a small harness for live assertions and synthetic telemetry. No breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: teach engineers common retrieval+generation patterns through an interactive cookbook rather than a single monolithic quickstart. This PR adds a short, opinionated set of recipes that demonstrate: (1) multi-index retrieval (per-tenant + global), (2) prefix/kv cache warmup for chat sessions, (3) incremental index updates with delta ingestion, and (4) stepwise live assertions to guard quality regressions during authoring. The goal is developer onboarding: readers should be able to open a notebook, run the cells locally (or in CodeSandbox), and see telemetry probes and pass/fail assertions that highlight model drift or retrieval regressions.

What I changed: added docs + runnable examples under docs/rag-recipe-cookbook and examples/rag-recipe-notebook. Included a short authoring guide (index.md), a Jupyter notebook (recipe.ipynb) with cell outputs trimmed for repository size, a lightweight Node-based harness (tools/assert-harness.ts) that runs assertions against a small prompt set, and a telemetry shim (telemetry/synthetic-probes.js) that emits example metrics to the Redwood Console format. Also added a small section to the Quickstarts TOC and updated the docs sidebar to surface the cookbook under "Authoring & Quickstarts > RAG Recipes".

Checklist: - [x] Add documentation page with background and step-by-step recipes - [x] Provide runnable notebook and minimal Node harness - [x] Include example telemetry probes and instructions for wiring to the Console - [x] Add low-friction local run instructions (npm / pip stub) - [x] Add short smoke tests to CI to ensure the example notebook executes without error (cell outputs mocked)

Usage notes: the notebook defaults to using an ephemeral in-memory index; for realistic runs the authoring guide shows how to switch to a Redwood-managed index or an S3-backed index. The harness includes two assertion types: exact-match for deterministic tool outputs (useful for indexed metadata) and fuzzy similarity for generated text (cosine threshold). The telemetry shim is intentionally small — it demonstrates the Console ingestion format and how labels/dimensions map to SDK tags.

Backward compatibility and scope: purely additive doc/examples. No changes to public APIs or runtime. There is a small test that runs a headless snippet via node and asserts that the example flow completes; that test is placed under docs/smoke and uses CI-provided mock tokens to avoid secrets in CI.

Related: follows conversations in ENG-3281 about surfacing authoring best practices and addresses DOC-114 request for more end-to-end examples for multi-index patterns.

A few requests: make the fuzzy threshold configurable and add a short snippet showing how to switch to Redwood-managed index." - Priya (author): "Addressed: added an env var and a short section in authoring-guide.md explaining Redwood index wiring. Also added a note about cost implications of dense indexes." - Marta Ruiz (review): "Please ensure the notebook cells are trimmed and CI doesn't try to render heavy outputs." - Priya: "Notebook trimmed; added a mocked-run path used by CI to execute without heavy artifacts." - Jonah Park (approval): "Approach LGTM, small nits left, but can be fixed post-merge." - Evan Li: "Approved after fuzzy threshold made configurable and tests green.",

CI checks: ["ci/docs-lint: pass", "ci/notebook-smoke: pass (uses mocked python env)", "ci/links-check: pass", "ci/telemetry-smoke: pass"]. One flaky failure occurred on first run for ci/notebook-smoke (cell execution timed out); I increased the timeout and added a mocked-run mode. Rerun passed.

Merge outcome: merged via squash with commit message: "docs(rag-cookbook): add interactive recipes, notebook, assertion harness and telemetry shim — closes ENG-3281, DOC-114". No changelog entry required beyond release notes because this is docs-only.

Testing notes for maintainers: the smoke runner is shell-scripted and safe to run locally; it requires Node 18+ for the harness and Python 3.10+ for notebook execution. CI uses a lightweight mocked environment; see docs/rag-recipe-cookbook/authoring-guide.md for reproduction steps. If you want the full notebook outputs you can run examples/rag-recipe-notebook/recipe.ipynb with the provided requirements.txt; be mindful of token usage if you wire to live models.
